title: Checkpointed output validation and tool backpressure acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD: Define acceptance criteria for an incremental validation mode that emits checkpoint markers during long structured streams and specifies runtime behavior when downstream tool invocations are throttled or fail. This ticket clarifies scope and success measures for the PM + Eng + Design deliverable: a deterministic runtime contract for partial structured emissions, a consumer-friendly error/fallback envelope, and operational backpressure signals for tool gateways.
background: Customers building multi-step pipelines require: 1) confidence that partial structured output can be validated incrementally without blocking the entire stream, and 2) predictable runtime semantics when a tool endpoint is temporarily overloaded or rate-limited. Current behavior is inconsistent across models and runtimes; we must standardize envelopes, checkpoint cadence, and a graceful fallback strategy so product owners can reason about correctness and recovery.
out_of_scope: Offline batch validation of completed objects, complex schema negotiation protocols between heterogeneous tool ecosystems, and crypto-level signing of partial emissions (may be separate security ticket).
risks: 1) Too-frequent checkpoints increase token overhead and cost. 2) Ambiguous fallback semantics can surface as silent data loss. 3) Tool gateway backpressure may interact poorly with existing request-level SLOs and autoscaling policies.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Checkpoint envelope markers are emitted at configurable intervals (by byte or token count) and are discoverable by consumers. Each checkpoint is a single JSON-line with a stable envelope key 'checkpoint_v1' and contains: sequence_id, byte_offset, partial_schema_hash, timestamp, and optional 'continuation_hint'.

AC-2: Partial structured emissions must include a minimal provenance header at the start of the stream: {stream_id, model_version, validation_mode} where validation_mode is one of [off, lightweight, strict]. The header is the first emitted line and parsers must tolerate its absence only when validation_mode is 'off'.

AC-3: For 'lightweight' validation_mode the runtime must validate only top-level shape at each checkpoint (field presence and types) and emit a 'validation_summary' line alongside the checkpoint with counts of passed/failed checks. For 'strict' mode the runtime must run full schema validation for the object fragment and surface an immediate 'validation_error' envelope if checks fail, including error codes from the validator.

AC-4: Tool invocation envelope: when a tool call is emitted mid-stream, the runtime must wrap the call intent in a 'tool_call_v1' envelope that includes idempotency_key, tool_name, expected_response_schema, and fallback_policy. Consumers must be able to replay or deduplicate calls using idempotency_key.

AC-5: Backpressure semantics: when the tool gateway returns a transient overload or 429, the runtime must: 1) emit a 'tool_backpressure' checkpoint with retry_after_seconds; 2) pause further tool-call emissions for the stream for the advertised window; 3) switch subsequent dependent outputs into a 'deferred' state (marked in envelopes) so downstream consumers can decide to wait or resume; and 4) log metrics that increment a 'tool.backpressure_events' counter for the tool and stream_id.

AC-6: Fallback behavior: if a tool remains unavailable beyond a configurable threshold (default 30s), the runtime must follow the fallback_policy in the tool_call envelope: one of ['skip', 'noop', 'synthetic_stub', 'abort_stream']. For 'synthetic_stub' the runtime must annotate that the content is estimated and include a 'confidence' score. 'abort_stream' must emit a final 'stream_aborted' envelope with failure code and human-readable reason.

AC-7: Streaming compatibility: all envelopes must be newline-delimited JSON lines and parsers must tolerate interleaved 'text' chunks and envelopes. Envelopes must be unambiguous (start with envelope_type field). The runtime must never emit partial JSON objects that break line-delimited semantics.

AC-8: Observability and debugability: each stream must emit a periodic 'health_tick' envelope (configurable cadence) that contains token_rate and outstanding_tool_calls count. There must be dashboard panels showing per-tool backpressure rate and per-model checkpoint overhead.
implementation_notes: Eng to implement envelope producer and validator library in rw-runtime (C++/Rust binding) plus SDK decoders in Node/Python. Design to supply envelope wire spec and UX copy for Console. PM to own rollout plan and backward compatibility migration (default validation_mode=off).
qa_test_plan: 1) Unit tests for envelope serialization and parser resilience to interleaved text/envelope lines. 2) End-to-end tests against a mock tool gateway that returns configurable 429/500 patterns to verify backpressure pause/resume and fallback_policy outcomes. 3) Load test to measure checkpoint cost delta at T=1k concurrent streams.
